newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues rules on trading by brokers.
newsitem.headline: China issues rules on trading by brokers.

text.p: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has issued regulations on trading by stockbrokers on their own account, the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.
It called the regulations, which have already come into effect, a major step in building the legal and regulatory framework for China's securities markets.
The bankruptcy of Barings, the Daiwa Bank scandal and the 1995 treasury bond futures trading scandal in China showed the importance of risk control and regulatory supervision, the newspaper said.
The regulations state that stocks held by a brokerage must not exceed 80 percent of its net assets or capital used for stock trading, based on the prices at which it bought the stocks, it said.
The debt-net asset ratio of a brokerage must not exceed a ratio of 10:1, it said.
Working capital of a brokerage doing stock trading on its own account must not be less than 50 percent of its net assets or of its capital used for stock trading, it said.
Except for treasury bonds, the holdings by a brokerage of one stock must not exceed 20 percent of its total stockholdings, based on the price at which it purchased the shares, it said.

A brokerage must put aside five percent of its profits from stock trading into a risk fund until the fund reaches five percent of its net assets or capital working for stock trading and maintain that level, it said.
These percentages can be adjusted by the CSRC according to circumstances, it said.
Brokerages must set up their own departments to do risk management and internal investigations, it said.
The regulations outlaw insider trading, market manipulation and improper use of different accounts to cause abnormal price movements, it said.
One analyst said that the rules were an important step and would help to check irregularities that had occurred in the past for lack of clear national regulations.
"In the past, risk control supervision were very loose. Stockbrokerages went bankrupt but did not have to announce the fact. These rules will help to improve the security of brokerages," he said.
